items.headline: Update: Singapore and China launch talks to upgrade their free trade pact after Wong-Xi meeting
items.summary: After meeting President Xi Jinping on Nov 20 following the APEC summit, PM Lawrence Wong said Singapore and China have begun negotiations to upgrade their bilateral free trade agreement, with the refresh set to cover areas such as the digital economy.

items.headline: Pre-school teacher, 59, jailed for slapping a five-year-old girl with autism
items.summary: A 59-year-old pre-school teacher was sentenced to three weeks' jail on Nov 20 for slapping a five-year-old girl with autism who was singing herself to sleep, The Straits Times reported.

items.headline: Australian woman, 56, to be charged after allegedly shoving ICA officers at Changi Airport
items.summary: A 56-year-old Australian woman allegedly pushed Immigration & Checkpoints Authority officers, hurled vulgarities and slapped an officer's thigh at Changi Airport; she faces charges, Mothership reported.

items.headline: Father and son jailed after flying from China to assault a man over a failed S$18,000 deal
items.summary: A father and son were each jailed 10 weeks after flying from China to Singapore to assault a Malaysian businessman over a failed S$18,000 investment, Mothership reported.

items.headline: India's opposition protests outside Meta offices over Instagram account suspensions
items.summary: Youth Congress activists protested outside Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram on Nov 21 over suspended Instagram accounts belonging to journalists, creators and government critics, issuing a seven-day ultimatum; two accounts were restored but thousands remain restricted.

items.headline: Toxic alcohol kills at least 11 and hospitalises about 180 in Manipur
items.summary: At least 11 people died and about 180 were taken to hospital after drinking suspected spurious alcohol traced to Manipur's Sugnu area; the chief minister ordered an inquiry and vowed those responsible would be arrested.

items.headline: Nikhil Gupta sentenced to 19 years in the US over plot to kill separatist Pannun
items.summary: A Manhattan federal court sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months - about 19 years - on Nov 20 for a foiled murder-for-hire plot against Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun; India has denied any government involvement.

items.headline: Modi urges Indian companies to chase global markets as inflation and the rupee bite
items.summary: PM Narendra Modi on Nov 19 urged Indian firms to look beyond the home market and pursue global demand, as retail inflation runs above the central bank's 6% ceiling and the rupee hovers near record lows against the dollar.

items.headline: UK far-right activist 'Danny Tommo' jailed for slashing a Channel migrant boat
items.summary: A UK court jailed far-right activist 'Danny Tommo' for slashing an inflatable migrant boat, with the judge calling it a deliberate disruption of cross-Channel operations; in a separate case, Vickrum Digwa was jailed for life, minimum 21 years, for murdering 18-year-old student Henry Nowak.

items.headline: Milburn review urges Britain to spend now on youth unemployment to save billions later
items.summary: A long-awaited review led by Alan Milburn urged PM Andy Burnham's government to invest now in tackling youth unemployment, estimating its full package would deliver about GBP 13.7bn in welfare savings by 2036/37.

items.headline: Russia rules out any deal letting Ukraine join NATO as the US pushes Article 5 guarantees
items.summary: Deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov said on Nov 20 that Moscow rejects Ukraine's NATO membership - or any quasi-membership - in a peace deal, a day after US envoy Jared Kushner said Russia was 'comfortable' with Article 5-style security guarantees for Kyiv.

items.headline: Russian 'triple-tap' strike on Kryvyi Rih kills an emergency worker and a seven-year-old
items.summary: A Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih, President Zelensky's home city, killed an emergency worker and a seven-year-old child on Nov 21, Ukrainian officials said; the 'triple-tap' tactic hits the same site in succession to catch first responders.

items.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least four in Gaza as the US warns the truce could collapse
items.summary: Israeli attacks killed at least four Palestinians on Nov 21, including three near a vehicle distributing food aid, as winter flooding worsened conditions; the US-led Board of Peace warned the year-old ceasefire could collapse without action.

items.headline: COP31 climate talks run into overtime after a draft drops all mention of fossil fuels
items.summary: Nearly 200 nations blew past the deadline at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, deadlocked over a draft that dropped any mention of fossil fuels and a $120bn adaptation-finance target; the EU warned the text risked turning the summit into a 'fossil' COP and Panama threatened to walk out.

items.headline: Apple is reportedly building its own AI agent to operate your Mac
items.summary: Apple is developing an in-house AI agent that can autonomously carry out tasks on a Mac, TechCrunch reported on Nov 19, citing Bloomberg; the project is said to be early-stage, and a coming macOS update will warn users against giving third-party agents full access.

items.headline: A wave of AI agents that live inside your text messages arrives
items.summary: TechCrunch surveyed a crop of AI assistants that work entirely over SMS and chat apps - among them the pre-seed-funded Fambot - as startups race to put agents where people already message.

items.headline: Operator-led VC Plural raises $1.1 billion for European 'moonshots'
items.summary: Plural, the founder-led European VC behind defence firm Helsing, raised EUR 1bn (about $1.1bn) on Nov 15, splitting it between a third early-stage fund and a new follow-on fund targeting energy, AI infrastructure, defence and health.

items.headline: Crypto rout deepens as Bitcoin slides below $58,000
items.summary: Bitcoin fell below about $57,700 on Nov 21 - its first time there since September 2024 - heading for its longest weekly losing streak since 2022; the total crypto market has shrunk to roughly $2 trillion, about half its 2025 peak.

items.headline: SoftBank suffers its worst day in over two years as the AI selloff hits Asia
items.summary: SoftBank shares closed about 14.5% lower on Nov 20, their worst day since August 2024, helping drag Japan's Nikkei 225 down 5.06% to 56,436.65 as investors questioned AI-infrastructure returns after Anthropic's rocky market debut.

items.headline: Anthropic falls into the red on its second day of public trading
items.summary: Anthropic's stock dropped about 9% on Nov 20, giving back much of its debut-day pop, as a broad tech-wreck pulled AI names lower across the market.

items.headline: Gold slumps to its lowest level since September 2025
items.summary: Spot gold fell to about $3,518 an ounce on Nov 20, its lowest since September 2025 and down roughly 9.5% on the week, pressured by a firmer dollar, rising bets on a December Fed rate hike, and the AI-driven selloff.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen inherits Las Vegas pole after Antonelli's fastest lap draws a grid penalty
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli set the quickest time in Las Vegas qualifying but a five-place grid penalty for a power-unit change hands pole to Max Verstappen, with George Russell second and Lando Norris third; Oscar Piastri drops to 17th on a separate penalty. The race runs Sunday.

items.headline: 🏎️ Russell hits out at Verstappen after a Las Vegas qualifying clash
items.summary: George Russell accused Max Verstappen of impeding him in Las Vegas qualifying, saying 'somebody's got to stand up to that guy', while Mercedes boss Toto Wolff defended Russell's track position amid questions over a tow.

items.headline: 🎾 Alcaraz fights back past Shelton to reach the ATP Finals final
items.summary: Carlos Alcaraz recovered from a set down to beat Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) in Turin on Nov 21, reaching his second straight ATP Finals title match.

items.headline: 🎾 Zverev downs Medvedev in straight sets to set up an ATP Finals title clash with Alcaraz
items.summary: World No. 1 Alexander Zverev beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6(0), 6-4 on Nov 21 without dropping a set all week, setting up a Sunday final against Carlos Alcaraz; Zverev chases a third ATP Finals crown.

items.headline: 🏏 Update: India pile on 486-4 to lead New Zealand by 118 on day three in Wellington
items.summary: India reached 486 for 4 at stumps on day three of the first Test in Wellington - KL Rahul 136, Shubman Gill out for 98, Devdutt Padikkal 80 and Rishabh Pant 55 not out - to lead New Zealand's 368 by 118 runs.

items.headline: Mathematicians back an AI-generated proof of the Riemann hypothesis as a rival claim emerges
items.summary: Members of the Lean and Mathlib formal-proof communities said they have full confidence that an AI-generated proof of the Riemann hypothesis - long one of mathematics' biggest unsolved problems - is correct; the proof, posted by an Anthropic researcher, now faces a competing claim that a human may have reached a similar result first.

items.headline: A new study upends a 150-year-old model of how the brain produces language
items.summary: Brain-mapping research challenges a 150-year-old account of speech, finding that planning to speak draws on an 'auditory image' of a word's sounds in the temporal lobe rather than on Broca's area alone; the authors say the work could improve brain-computer interfaces for people who cannot speak.

items.headline: Viral 'vibe archaeology' claim that AI found a Maya site sparks a scientific firestorm
items.summary: A viral claim that AI had discovered an unmapped Maya site in Mexico unravelled after archaeologists pointed out the site had already been documented, fuelling a sharp debate over the promise - and the hype - of AI in scientific discovery.

items.headline: A new AI-aided Navier-Stokes proof reignites a math-world dispute
items.summary: Researchers unveiled a fresh AI-aided proof of 'blow-up' in the Navier-Stokes equations that govern fluid flow, reviving a dispute over an earlier OpenAI result that critics said had tackled a less meaningful variant of the problem.

fun_fact.headline: Lightning is about five times hotter than the Sun's surface
fun_fact.body: A bolt of lightning superheats the air in its path to roughly 30,000 kelvin - about five times hotter than the visible surface of the Sun, which sits near 5,800 kelvin. The air expands so fast that it creates a shock wave, and that shock wave is what we hear as thunder.

puzzle.title: Unfolded
puzzle.body: The six faces of a cube have been unfolded into a flat cross: A sits above C; the row B C D E runs left to right; and F sits below C. When the net is folded back into a cube, which single face ends up directly opposite face C?
puzzle.approach: Pick one square as the front, then fold the rest around it - or use the rule that in a straight strip of four faces, the two that are two apart end up opposite.
puzzle.answer: Face E. Fold C to be the front: A folds up (top), F folds down (bottom), B folds left, D folds right, and E - which hangs off D - wraps round to the back, directly opposite C. The three opposite pairs are C-E, B-D and A-F.

word_puzzle.title: On the Mend
word_puzzle.body: Turn SICK into WELL in four steps, changing one letter at a time; each intermediate word must be a valid English word.
word_puzzle.approach: Change exactly one letter at each step, keeping every rung a real word.
word_puzzle.answer: SICK -> SILK -> SILL -> SELL -> WELL (SILK: C to L; SILL: K to L; SELL: I to E; WELL: S to W). A 'sill' is the ledge beneath a window.

notes: Quiet-weekend, degraded-network run. Today is Sunday SGT; US and most global markets were closed for the weekend, so Business ran on the Fri Nov 20 close plus Sat Nov 21 crypto moves. The WebSearch crawler could not reach several allowed primary outlets (BBC, Sky News, Reuters, The Guardian, AP, NYT, CNA, The Straits Times, SCMP, The Verge, Ars Technica, New Scientist, all Indian primary outlets, Cricbuzz); WebFetch could not resolve any external host under the network policy, so research ran entirely through WebSearch on reachable allowed/fallback outlets (Mothership, Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, CNBC, TechCrunch, Sky Sports, Formula1.com, ATP Tour, ESPNcricinfo/ESPN, Nature, Scientific American). India ran on fallback sources (Al Jazeera, Bloomberg) as every primary Indian outlet was unreachable; it reached 4 verified items. UK News ran on the fallback tier (Al Jazeera, Bloomberg) as BBC and Sky News were unreachable, and yielded only 2 verified UK-domestic items on a quiet news weekend - fewer stories today, not padded. Tech & AI yielded 3 items (one, the Plural fund, from Nov 15) as fresh weekend product/company news was thin. Singapore (Mothership) reached 4. No spectrum blocks were used because three distinct real-outlet framings could not be sourced under the network restrictions. F1: Las Vegas qualifying (Verstappen on pole after Antonelli's penalty) was confirmed current against Formula1.com/Sky; the race had NOT run at publish time, so no race result was reported. Cricket: no deep-link ESPNcricinfo match URL was indexable, so the day-three scorecard (scores corroborated across ESPN/ESPNcricinfo reports) links to the ESPNcricinfo WTC fixtures hub, as on prior days. Total verified items across the brief: 30 (well above the 8-item hard-stop). About 28 searches and multiple retries were made.
